skills.name: Special days, national days and public holidays

note.text:
Public holidays in Cameroon include New Year's Day (1 January), Youth Day (11 February), Labour Day (1 May), National Day (20 May), Assumption Day (15 August) and Christmas Day (25 December), and religious holidays whose dates change: Good Friday, Ascension Day, Eid al-Fitr (the end of Ramadan) and Eid al-Adha (the Feast of the Ram).
On National Day we celebrate the unity of Cameroon; on Youth Day young people march; on Labour Day workers march.
Special family days: birthdays, weddings, naming ceremonies.
Talking about holidays: “What do you do on National Day?” — “I march with my school.” “Happy New Year!” “Merry Christmas!” “Happy birthday!”
Names of holidays begin with capital letters.

worked_example.problem: Write three sentences about {d}: when it is, what people do, and what you say.
steps: What people do: Pupils and students march past the grandstand, and there are speeches and games.
worked_example.answer: {d} is in {m}. Pupils march past the grandstand. People say “Happy {d}!”

cards.idea: Read the dialogue about National Day.
example: Tabe: Why is there no school on Thursday?
Manka: It's the twentieth of May, National Day. We celebrate the unity of Cameroon.
Tabe: Are you going to march?
Manka: Yes, our school will march past the grandstand. Then my family will have a big lunch.
Tabe: I marched on Youth Day in February. Which holiday do you like best?
Manka: Christmas! But I also enjoy the Feast of the Ram with my Muslim neighbours.

pick.q: Why is there no school on Thursday?
e: The dialogue says it is National Day.
pick.y: Manka says it is the twentieth of May, National Day.

pick.q: What do people celebrate on National Day?
pick.y: Manka says we celebrate the unity of Cameroon.

e: Manka will march on National Day.
The dialogue does not say that.
The dialogue does not say that.
pick.y: Tabe says he marched on Youth Day in February.

pick.q: Which holiday does Manka like best?
e: She talks about it, but likes Christmas best.

cards.idea: Each national day has its own date and meaning.
example: National Day, the {20} of May: the unity of Cameroon.
Youth Day, the {11} of February: young people march.

cards.idea: Use the right greeting for each special day. Names of holidays start with capital letters.

questions.prompt: Match each holiday to its date.

e: That is for someone who is ill.
pick.y: On Christmas Day we say Merry Christmas!
On 1 January we say Happy New Year!

pick.q: to a friend on her birthday
e: That is for someone who has died.
pick.y: On a birthday we say Happy birthday!

pick.q: to Muslim neighbours on Eid al-Fitr
pick.y: On Eid we wish a happy feast: Eid Mubarak!

pick.q: On which day do workers march?
e: On Youth Day young people march.
pick.y: Labour Day is the workers' day.

pick.q: Which holiday celebrates the unity of Cameroon?
e: Assumption Day is a Christian feast.
New Year's Day starts the year.

pick.q: Which holiday marks the end of Ramadan?
e: Eid al-Adha is the Feast of the Ram.
Good Friday is a Christian holiday.
Youth Day is a national holiday.
pick.y: Eid al-Fitr ends the fasting month of Ramadan.

pick.q: Why do the dates of Good Friday and Eid change every year?
pick.y: Religious holidays follow the Christian and Islamic calendars.

questions.prompt: One sentence has a mistake. Which one?

right.text: We say Merry Christmas on 25 December.

wrong.text: We celebrated national day with a march.
wrong.explain: Names of holidays start with capital letters: National Day.
Youth Day is on 11 February; 25 December is Christmas.

wrong.text: Labour Day is the feast of the Ram.
wrong.explain: Labour Day is for workers; the Feast of the Ram is Eid al-Adha.
